newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila trade minister denies devaluation report.
newsitem.headline: Manila trade minister denies devaluation report.

text.p: Philippine Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista on Wednesday denied a newspaper report that devaluation of the peso would be discussed in today's Monetary Board meeting.
"I never said that. This is certainly a misrepresentation of what I said," he told Reuters.
Bautista, who is also a member of the Monetary Board, said "I'm not in favour of a devaluation."

The Singapore Straits Times report said: "The Philippine central bank's Monetary Board is meeting today to take up a proposal to devalue the peso, Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista told the Straits Times yesterday."

The report did not have any direct quotes mentioning devaluation but said: "'We already wrote a letter to the governor. It will be taken up during the meeting,' said Bautista, who is a member of the seven-man board."
Denying the report, Bautista said: "It's not on the agenda."
He said business groups demanding a weaker peso in order to boost Philippine exports were meant to submit their proposal to the Central Bank.
Last Friday, businessmen and key government economic officials had a dialogue with President Fidel Ramos to discuss ways to enhance the Philippines' competitivess in the world market.
The businessmen had urged for a gradual depreciation of the peso, but Ramos said the matter should be referred to the Central Bank, which is independent of the executive branch.
